title: Mujadara
subtitle: Lebanese lentils and rice with caramelised onions
excerpt: A simple, deeply satisfying dish of green lentils and rice cooked together, topped with very slowly caramelised onions that go sweet, dark, and almost crispy. One of the great cheap vegetarian suppers.

recipe.sourceNotes: Mujadara is one of the oldest recorded dishes in the Middle East, with references appearing in medieval Arab cookbooks. It is widespread across Lebanon, Syria, Jordan, Palestine, and Egypt, with regional variations in the lentil-to-rice ratio and spicing.

content.text: Mujadara is lentils and rice cooked together until soft, then piled with dark, slow-caramelised onions. The onions are the part that takes time and patience, but they are the whole flavour of the dish. It is served at room temperature with yoghurt and a simple salad, and it is one of those dishes that tastes more than the sum of its parts.
Put the lentils in a saucepan with 600 ml of the water. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes. They should be almost but not completely cooked through.

Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat. Add the sliced onions with a good pinch of salt. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 35 to 40 minutes until deeply golden and almost jammy. Turn the heat low if they are colouring too quickly. Do not rush this step.

Add the rinsed rice to the lentils. Add the remaining 300 ml water, the cumin, cinnamon, salt, and pepper. Stir together. Bring to a boil, cover tightly with a lid, and cook over the lowest possible heat for 20 minutes.
Remove from the heat and leave to steam, lid on, for 10 minutes. Uncover, fluff gently with a fork, and taste for seasoning.
Serve the lentil-rice piled on a platter, topped with most of the caramelised onions and their oil. Scatter the rest of the onions over the top. Serve warm or at room temperature with yoghurt.
